subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call?
rationale: The issue touches sandboxed execution semantics and the report explicitly allows either warning or error behavior, so automation should not choose a stricter security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a non-sandbox or elevated path.

options.title: Adopt Fork After Decision
options.body: Review the open fork PR only after deciding whether warning-only behavior is the intended product/security policy.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history signal for original exec PTY behavior and adjacent fallback semantics.
